title: Hadosh Academy Canonical Abstraction Library
purpose: A shared, framework-agnostic context for understanding and building local, inspectable, user-owned AI harnesses. Each term gives people and agents one current meaning to work from.

definitionStates.consolidated: Accepted as shared context for new work.

terms.name: Model
terms.definition: In Hadosh Academy, a model is the parametric information-processing compartment of an agentic system and the category to which large language models belong. Its learned capabilities, representations, tendencies, knowledge, memory, and any reasoning performed in parameter or latent space are encoded in or produced through its parameters. A model receives supplied context, performs inference, and returns model-originated output to that shared interface. The output may be language, media, a prediction, classification, score, probability, representation, structured decision, action proposal, reasoning trace, or another inferred result. A model may be commercial, open-weight, provider-hosted, private, local, general, specialized, or fine-tuned to operate a harness. Architecture, training data and method, size, context capacity, modality, provider, and deployment affect a particular model’s capabilities without defining the compartment. Hadosh Academy treats model capability as a replaceable utility: powerful and necessary, but not the complete agentic system. Its utility becomes effective through interaction with a harness. A model may contain parametric memory and may generate explicit reasoning. When reasoning remains in latent or parameter space, it remains model-side. When it is emitted as text or another inspectable representation, it enters context and can be surrounded by harness mechanisms. A model output can propose or describe an action, but it is not by itself proof of truth, authorization, execution, verification, or completion. The boundary is intentionally practical rather than a claim that every system must distribute cognition identically. It lets people locate parametric behavior, evaluate it independently, replace it, and avoid assigning it responsibilities that another compartment can perform more reliably.

terms.name: Large language model (LLM)
terms.definition: A large language model, or LLM, is a model trained to predict or generate language tokens from context. Additional training may help it follow instructions, select tools, produce structured output, or perform reasoning-like operations. In a harness, the LLM can interpret context and propose what should happen next, but fluent output does not prove factual correctness, permission, execution, or completion. The LLM is therefore treated as a replaceable, probabilistic capability—not as the agent, its memory, or its authority. The harness supplies durable context, state, tools, permissions, and verification around it. Future models may use different outputs or internalize more procedure, but practical agency still requires a governed connection between learned capability and action.
openQuestions: Which guarantees must always remain outside LLM discretion even when structured output becomes more reliable?
When does the narrower term LLM stop being useful and the broader term model become the better abstraction?
How should this definition cover multimodal models whose language interface is only one part of their capability?

terms.name: Decision model
terms.definition: A decision model is a model exposed through a bounded interface that evaluates supplied state against caller-defined questions and returns typed judgments with declared uncertainty for use inside explicit software logic. A judgment may estimate whether a condition holds, choose among defined options, rank candidates, score an ordered rubric, or use another bounded form whose meaning is declared by the caller. The term describes the model’s interface and role in a harness, not one internal architecture: a specialized model, large language model, ensemble, or future learned system may realize the interface. Typed output constrains shape, not truth. The harness selects and minimizes the state, defines the questions and criteria, validates the returned schema, interprets probabilities or scores through explicit policy, handles ambiguity, abstention, timeout, and failure, and retains authority over side effects. A decision model can supply one inference step inside a hook or workflow, but it does not by itself verify a claim, authorize an action, execute a transition, or own source-of-truth state.
openQuestions: What minimum output contract distinguishes a decision model from a general model returning arbitrary structured JSON?
How should calibration and abstention expectations be represented without assuming that every provider has demonstrated them?
Which automatic consequences may responsibly depend on a probabilistic judgment, and which parts of that boundary belong in a separate behavioral pattern?

terms.name: Runtime
terms.definition: A runtime is active execution machinery that turns stored capability and harness structure into running behavior. Because the word is overloaded, Hadosh Academy qualifies it when the distinction matters. A model runtime executes or provides model inference. An agent runtime activates and orchestrates harness mechanisms around that capability: it assembles selected context, carries sessions or events, exposes permitted tools, invokes models, applies available control points, and returns results and evidence for verification. A runtime is not the complete harness; durable instructions, memory, jobs, identity, authority, and history can remain while no runtime is active. A command-line interface may launch, attach to, or control a runtime, but the interface is not itself the execution machinery. Model and agent runtimes may be local, hosted, distributed, embedded, or composed across services. Their location, custody, enforcement capabilities, and failure boundaries should be explicit. Instructions can request behavior, but only runtime or other deterministic harness mechanisms can guarantee a block, protected action, atomic update, or enforced permission boundary.
openQuestions: How should model-runtime and agent-runtime responsibility be reported when inference, orchestration, tools, and state span several services?
Which enforcement capabilities are necessary before an agent runtime can honestly support consequential action?
Which continuity state belongs to an active runtime, and which must remain in the durable harness so the agent can recover after execution stops?

terms.name: Harness
terms.definition: In Hadosh Academy, a harness is the non-parametric information-processing compartment around model capability. It is composed from explicit, inspectable structures such as text, files, commands, code, rules, hooks, jobs, state, tools, permissions, workflows, interfaces, tests, histories, and recovery mechanisms. It constructs and supplies context to models, receives model-originated output, and determines what is interpreted, stored, removed, routed, executed, verified, rejected, or returned in later context. The harness turns model inference into continuing, bounded, and effective work. It can preserve durable memory, identity, responsibilities, authority, evidence, corrections, methods, and accumulated experience while models are replaced or assigned to different jobs, phases, or subtasks. A tool-call output is model inference; the software that authorizes and performs the call is harness behavior. A conditional hook that injects information is harness memory combined with a trigger. Harnesses may be thin or extensive, local or distributed, provider-controlled or user-controlled, textual or heavily coded, and they may surround different stages of cognition, including exposed reasoning traces. Hadosh Academy does not prescribe one universal configuration. It favors arrangements that move durable customization, inspectability, intervention, recovery, and practical control toward the user’s own harness. A harness does not replace parametric inference, and more structure is not automatically better. Its components are separated so their logic, state, authority, failures, and effects can be evaluated and improved independently. The filesystem is a current practical body for this durable structure, not the only possible implementation. The defining role is the non-parametric organization that carries the user’s relationship, continuity, and control around replaceable model capability.

terms.name: Plugin
terms.definition: A plugin is a bounded, composable, separately improvable harness module with one scoped responsibility. It may contribute instructions, context selection or injection, state, triggers or hooks, tool adapters, permission relationships, lifecycle rules, outputs, and verification, but no single file shape or mechanism is required. The runtime may load, invoke, or provide control points for a plugin; runtime, hook, and plugin are not synonyms. The harness retains the surrounding authority, routing, and source-of-truth boundaries, while the plugin owns only its declared scope. A dependable plugin makes its inputs, state, effects, failure behavior, and evidence inspectable enough to remove, replace, or adapt it without silently redefining the rest of the agent. Plugin portability therefore lives first in its responsibility and behavioral contract. Its concrete hooks, commands, files, APIs, and event wiring may remain runtime-specific.
openQuestions: What minimum separability or removability distinguishes a plugin from an internal harness component?
Which parts of plugin anatomy must be declared before its behavioral contract can be adapted across runtimes?
How should a plugin's authority remain bounded when it registers hooks, exposes tools, or updates shared harness state?

terms.name: Agent
terms.definition: An agent is a persistent, bounded, governed system formed from model capability and a harness with durable identity, responsibilities, state, authority, tools, memory, and verification. The term names the composed system, not the model, harness, runtime, interface, or one conversation alone. Its identity can persist while no runtime is active because the harness can preserve the structures that make its responsibilities and history distinct. When an agent runtime activates that composition with selected context, the result is an active agent session or instance. One agent may therefore continue across restarts, model substitutions, and several interfaces, while one model can animate many distinct agents. An agent can interpret supplied state, propose or make bounded decisions, use permitted tools, update owned state, communicate, and advance work only within the authority and stopping conditions established by the user and harness. It should extend the user’s agency rather than silently becoming the owner of the user’s purposes.
openQuestions: What makes one bounded responsibility a distinct agent rather than a job, plugin, or component inside a larger agent?
What durable identity evidence distinguishes a dormant agent from a reusable harness template that has not yet been assigned responsibility?
How should cooperating sessions or model roles be described when they share one agent identity and authority boundary?

terms.name: Agency
terms.definition: Agency is the capacity to form purposes, make judgments, and cause directed change. In Hadosh Academy, externalized agency means that part of a person’s practical capacity is expressed through a harness they can understand and govern. A useful harness helps the user preserve decisions, sustain responsibilities, apply learned methods, inspect consequences, and intervene when needed. Agent activity is not automatically user agency: more autonomous execution can reduce agency when visibility, correction, ownership, or the ability to stop are lost. The goal is therefore expanded human capacity, with the user retaining authorship and authority while the harness carries more of the operational burden.
openQuestions: Which observable signs show that a harness is expanding a person’s agency rather than only increasing automated activity?
How should shared or organizational agency be distinguished from individual agency?
What minimum understanding and intervention ability must the user retain for agency to remain meaningfully theirs?

terms.name: Context
terms.definition: In Hadosh Academy, context is the active, bidirectional interface through which a model and harness influence one another. It is the bounded working surface containing information supplied for inference and the model-generated output returned from inference. At any moment, context is a mixture of harness-originated material—such as instructions, injections, retrieved memory, observations, tool results, state, constraints, and authority—and model-originated material—such as continuations, questions, reasoning traces, decisions, and action proposals. The harness constructs context by selecting, arranging, adding, removing, and formatting explicit information. The model interprets that context and extends or transforms it through inference. The harness then decides what model-generated material to display, persist, validate, execute, condense, reuse, or discard. This makes influence bidirectional without collapsing the two compartments: the harness influences the model through what it supplies, and the model influences the harness through what it generates. Context is not identical to memory or to a complete transcript. Parametric memory can influence output without appearing explicitly in context. Harness memory can remain stored without being loaded. Model-originated material can become harness state when it is deliberately preserved, while harness state can temporarily enter context when selected for an invocation. Provenance should remain visible even when material crosses the boundary. Different systems may expose different portions of cognition. Latent reasoning that never crosses the interface remains model-side; textual or otherwise inspectable reasoning that is exposed enters context and can be managed by local or provider-controlled harnesses. The purpose of the context boundary is not to impose one configuration, but to make the location and movement of information inspectable enough to evaluate and improve.

terms.name: Local
terms.definition: Local describes a harness layer operating within infrastructure the user directly controls, rather than existing only inside an external provider’s hidden application state. Locality can improve custody, inspectability, continuity, recovery, and the ability to replace providers. It does not automatically mean offline, private, secure, open-source, or completely self-hosted. A local harness may still call a remote model or service. Locality must therefore be described layer by layer: context can be local while inference is remote, and execution can be local while credentials or notifications depend on hosted systems. The practical question is what the user controls and what disappears when a dependency is removed.
openQuestions: Which layer must be under direct user control before a system can be described publicly as local?
How should partially local systems communicate remote inference, logging, connectors, and hosted state without misleading users?
Does user-operated remote infrastructure belong inside this definition or require a separate term?

terms.name: User-owned
terms.definition: A harness layer is user-owned when the user has durable custody and practical authority to inspect, modify, copy, recover, move, and dispose of it without depending entirely on one provider’s permission. Access alone is not ownership, and export alone is not operational portability. Ownership must be assessed by layer because data, context, instructions, code, execution, credentials, history, interfaces, and deployment may have different custodians. Meaningful ownership lets accumulated methods, state, corrections, and working history remain the user’s asset even when models, runtimes, or providers change. Shared harnesses require explicit governance rather than pretending that one individual owns collective state.
openQuestions: What minimum combination of custody, authority, portability, and recoverability justifies the term user-owned?
How should ownership be described when an organization, family, or community governs the harness collectively?
Which provider dependencies are compatible with meaningful ownership, and which make the claim misleading?

terms.name: Seed
terms.definition: A seed is the smallest coherent context or substrate from which a distinct harness can grow through use. It gives a person and agent enough shared language, boundaries, and developmental direction to begin without pre-deciding the mature system. A seed is not a miniature finished agent. Additional structure should be earned by real responsibilities, evidence, and user decisions. A seed may be primarily contextual, as in this library, or may include a minimal executable substrate. Hadosh Academy provides the starting abstractions; each user and agent decide how those abstractions become files, behaviors, tools, permissions, and interfaces in their own harness.
openQuestions: What minimum coherent content must a context seed contain before an agent can begin adapting it safely?
Which additions make a seed prematurely prescriptive rather than usefully orienting?
How should contextual seeds and executable seeds share a name without collapsing their different roles?
